terms.title: Aurora
terms.guideSubtitle: Operants, ExLAW and the powers behind them, for the Legend Dynamics RPG system
terms.facility: A hospital with an Operant ward
terms.journalIntro: Write it together at the end of each case. Advancements apply to the GM's copies; use each card's Save character file to send a player their update.
terms.emptyNote: Empty: it won't fire until you reload.
terms.otherWeapon: Another weapon or a power (nothing spent)
terms.tracksIntro: Shared by the whole team. Wrecked property and hurt bystanders, official attention and public anger each mark a box; clean arrests, good press and lying low clear one between cases.
terms.restrictedToggle: Show the Shadow Earth defector (only with the GM's permission)
terms.restrictedCheck: needs the GM's permission: tick the box in step 2 if your GM agreed

roles.name: ExLAW Agent
roles.text: ExLAW agent: a full-time federal agent of the Extraordinary Law Enforcement Agency (ExLAW), enforcing the Extraordinary Powers Act with a badge that opens doors and an EPAOC file that never closes.

roles.name: Officer
roles.text: Officer: carries a badge and the law's authority, working alongside ExLAW or around it: an FBI agent or U.S. marshal, an elected county sheriff (maybe on the edge of the Mad Fringe), a city cop first on the scene of an Operant fight, a detective, or a licensed private eye. Your Allegiance says which force you serve.

roles.name: Aegis Pilot
roles.text: Aegis pilot: flies the armored power suit that is the government's answer to Operants, and knows exactly what it costs per hour.

roles.name: International Operative
roles.text: International operative: Interpol, the French Affaires spéciales or MI5; the law has borders, Operants don't.

roles.name: Vigilante
roles.text: Vigilante: fights crime on the streets, unsanctioned and masked, and hopes ExLAW keeps looking the other way.

roles.name: Public Hero
roles.text: Public hero: famous, sponsored and televised, like the New Power Legion; the cameras are part of the job.

roles.name: Guardian
roles.text: Guardian: protects one place or one people (a neighborhood, a reservation, the Haven) and answers to them first.

roles.name: Crusader
roles.text: Crusader: sworn to an order or a cause, like the Shadow Knights; the vow comes before the law.

roles.name: Avenger
roles.text: Avenger: answers one kind of wrong, whatever the law says, as Uathach does.

roles.name: Scientist
roles.text: Scientist: studies Operants, metatropic fields or the breaches, for a university, a corporation or a government that won't say why.

roles.name: Occultist
roles.text: Occultist: an Earth Warden or a scholar of the hidden world, who knows which doors should stay shut.

roles.name: Doctor
roles.text: Doctor: treats what hospitals can't, Operant or not, and doesn't ask for a registration number.

roles.name: Relic Hunter
roles.text: Relic hunter: tracks down artifacts before the Foundation does, and sometimes before their owners notice.

roles.name: Journalist
roles.text: Journalist: reporter, blogger or documentary maker chasing the Operant story the public isn't being told.

roles.name: Mercenary
roles.text: Mercenary: powers or skills for hire, with a code or without one.

roles.name: Fugitive
roles.text: Fugitive: escaped from a lab or a cell; staying free is a full-time job.

roles.name: Activist
roles.text: Activist: fights for a cause the law won't touch (the Haven, the environment, Operant rights) on the street and on camera.

roles.name: Thief
roles.text: Thief: burglar, cat burglar or safecracker; powers make the impossible jobs possible.

roles.name: Con Artist
roles.text: Con artist: grifter and impostor; illusions and telepathy are tools of the trade.

roles.name: Enforcer
roles.text: Enforcer: muscle for a gang, a cartel or the Morcain.

roles.name: Smuggler
roles.text: Smuggler: moves people and cargo (relics, Ambrosia, refugees for the Haven) where the law can't see.

roles.name: Hacker
roles.text: Hacker: breaks into systems: corporate, police, the EMD itself.

roles.name: Fixer
roles.text: Fixer: knows everyone, moves anything, owes and is owed.

skills: Lie, bluff, disguise, forge, keep a secret identity
Informants, the underworld, black markets, rumors
Cameras, the press, social media, public image
Judge motives, spot a lie, interrogate
Search a scene, forensics, follow the money
The Extraordinary Powers Act, warrants, procedure, courts
Build, repair and modify machines, locks, Aegis suits
Magic, spirits, rituals, Otherworld and its creatures
Drive, fly, chase; pilot an Aegis suit
Aim, control and push your powers; perform rituals

origins.name: Non-Operant
origins.desc: No powers at all: training, nerve, gear and the law. Most of ExLAW's agents, every Aegis pilot and nearly everyone else on Earth. In a fight between Operants you are the one who has to be clever.
core: No powers: you need no registration (your legal status is usually Civilian, or Agent).
Aegis suits, power-dampening cuffs and good planning are how you stand beside Operants.
traits: +2 to Firearms or Brawling against an Operant whose powers you have studied.
Sometimes you're simply out of your depth. Accept the danger of staying in.
+2 to Investigation or Leadership to prepare for a known Operant's powers.
You've seen what Operants get away with. Accept the friction your bitterness causes.
+2 to Will against fear, mind powers and intimidation.
One good hit can end you. Accept the injury when you take a risk.

origins.name: Aurora-born
origins.desc: Powers that woke on their own: in the First Wave of April 1938, in the Second Wave of 1985, or inherited from a parent who was touched by either. The most common kind of Operant, and the one the EMD understands best.
core: Choose your wave: First Wave (awakened in 1938, or a direct descendant), Second Wave (1985) or a late bloomer whose powers woke without warning.
Your powers are part of you: they can't be taken away, only suppressed.
traits: +2 to Powers with your Class II power.
Your powers run in the family, and so do its enemies and debts. Accept the call.
+2 to Read People or Investigation to recognize another Operant and guess their power.
Your family has been in the EMD since 1952. Accept that ExLAW knows where you live.
Once per scene, push a power without marking Strain.
Everyone in your town knows what you can do. Accept the requests, the fear and the cameras.

origins.name: Ambrosia
origins.desc: Dosed with Ambrosia, the elixir Tesla's circle first refined: an idealized body, slowed aging and raw power. Rare, coveted and hunted; DIRE and the Foundation have both tried to make more.
core: Idealized: you age a year for every ten.
Ambrosia works on the body: Strength, Toughness, Flight, Speed, Regeneration and Transformation suit it best (the GM may allow others).
Coveted: every lab on Earth wants a sample of your blood.
traits: +2 to Persuasion or Media to inspire a crowd or a frightened person.
The power wants to be used. In your powered form, accept the flash of temper and what it costs.
Once per scene, ignore your injury penalties for one action.
Labs want what's in your veins. Accept the attempt.
+2 to Leadership with other heroes and with the public.
You've outlived friends and eras. Accept the grief and the gap.

origins.name: Lab-made
origins.desc: Made in a Foundation black lab, a DIRE program or somewhere worse. The powers are strong and unstable, the memories are patchy, and someone still has your file and wants their property back.
core: Unstable: on a natural 17 or 18 with Powers, mark a box of Strain as well.
Property: the lab that made you knows your powers better than you do.
traits: +2 to Powers when you push a power (you still mark Strain).
The lab hasn't given up. Accept the retrieval team.
Once per scene, a hit that would mark 2 or more boxes marks one fewer.
There are gaps in your memory, and someone else fills them. Accept the flashback at the worst moment.
+2 to Stealth or Read People to spot surveillance, restraints and traps.
Needles, labs and restraints break your nerve. Accept the panic.

origins.name: Bonded
origins.desc: Joined to something else: an artifact, a spirit, a god or an entity from beyond. It shares its power, and sometimes its mind. Michael Lance's amulet, Uathach's litany, the Ice Reaper and the Atomic Man are all bonds.
core: Choose the bond: an artifact you carry, or a spirit or entity that shares your body.
An artifact's powers go with the artifact; a spirit's come with its wants.
Bonded powers suit Transformation well: the bond is the alternate form.
traits: +2 to Occult or Investigation when your bond knows the answer (it remembers things you don't).
Your bond wants something you don't. Accept the choice it pushes on you.
Your bond resists for you: +2 to Will against mind powers and possession.
Your power lives in something that can be taken. Accept the theft or the trade.
+2 to Powers with the power your bond knows best.
Your bond had enemies long before you. Accept them as yours.

origins.name: Adept
origins.desc: A student of metatropic manipulation, the science everyone else calls magic. Learned rather than born, and growing with study: an Adept's own powers are few, but with time, materials and fuel a ritual can do almost anything.
core: Mystic powers: your own powers come from the mystic list (Cantrips, Warding, Summoning, Mystic Sight, Illusion, Blast, Portals, Astral Projection, Elemental Control, Teleport, Healing).
Rituals: you can emulate any power by ritual, with time, specialized materials and fuel (see Rituals).
Your second power is Class II once Powers is your top skill.
traits: +2 to Occult to identify a spell, a creature or a ritual's maker.
Something in Otherworld once helped you. Accept the favor it asks.
+2 to Powers when performing a ritual.
A forbidden text or a lost rite calls to you. Accept the detour.
+2 to Will against spirits, possession and fear.
The Earth Wardens, or older things, keep an eye on what you do. Accept the summons.

origins.name: Mythic
origins.desc: An ancient curse, blessing or bloodline: immortals, werewolves, the children of gods, warriors cursed by Jupiter. Mythic Operants are the oldest kind, and the hardest to classify.
core: GM's approval: every power a Mythic character takes, Immortality included, is agreed with the GM.
Only Mythic characters can take Immortality.
An old rule binds you: a curse's condition, a god's taboo or a bloodline's weakness, agreed with the GM.
traits: +2 to Occult or Persuasion where your myth is remembered.
Your curse or your god's taboo comes due. Accept its price.
+2 to Melee or Brawling against something as old as you.
The modern world baffles and offends you. Accept the misstep.
Once per scene, ignore your injury penalties for one action.
You don't die, but every wound hurts. Accept the pain that slows you.

origins.name: Otherworlder
origins.desc: Born outside this Earth: in a haven of Otherworld such as Avalon, or on a parallel Earth like Chat Roux's. Under the Extraordinary Powers Act you aren't a person at all, which makes you hard to register and easy to disappear.
core: Not a person under the Act: you can't register; you're Non-registered unless ExLAW makes you a deal.
Choose your world: Avalon (fey, Olympian and Asgardian descent), another haven, or a parallel Earth.
traits: +2 to Deception to pass as human or hide what you are.
You misread Earth's rules. Accept the misunderstanding.
+2 to Occult or Read People to see through illusions and disguises.
Iron burns you (fey-born) or your technology needs parts this Earth can't make. Accept the weakness.
+2 to Athletics to climb, leap or keep your footing.
Your home world wants you back, or wants you dead. Accept the envoy.

origins.name: Touched
origins.desc: Changed by an exposure to something nobody can name: a peyote vision in the desert, a ritual read aloud, a breach in the sky. Touched powers are strange, hard to classify and harder to control; the EMD files them under 'Other'.
core: Unclassifiable: the EMD can't tell what you are, and neither can you; the GM may give a power an odd limit or an odd extra.
Visions: once per case, the GM may give you a strange, true glimpse.
traits: +2 to Read People or Investigation when a vision points the way.
Your mind was burned by what you saw. Accept the episode at the worst moment.
+2 to Powers with your strangest power.
People sense something wrong about you. Accept the fear.
+2 to Will to keep calm when reality goes wrong.
Whatever touched you wants you back. Accept the pull.

origins.name: Shadow Earth Defector
origins.desc: A duplicate from Shadow Earth, the dark reflection of our world, who turned on its rulers and stayed. Somewhere on this Earth lives your original, who may not know you exist; Shadow Earth wants you back, and everyone else wants to know whose side you're on.
core: Your original: you are a copy of a real person on this Earth (agreed with the GM), and you share their face and their early memories.
Mystic Sight and Warding reveal what you are.
Needs the GM's permission.
traits: +2 to Deception or Investigation about your original's life and contacts.
Your original turns up, or someone mistakes you for them. Accept the trouble.
+2 to Occult to recognize Shadow Earth agents, duplicates and incursions.
Shadow Earth's rulers want their property back. Accept the duplicate sent for you.
+2 to Stealth in darkness and shadow.
Nobody trusts a copy. Accept the suspicion.

allegiances: exlaw
ExLAW
Once per case, a database search, an Aegis wing or federal backup.
Duty: the Director's orders, the EPAOC's questions and the paperwork.
fbi
A Federal Agency
Once per case, records, a lab or a warrant.
Duty: the agency's priorities, and its turf war with ExLAW.
sheriff
A County Sheriff's Office
Once per case, a deputy's help, the county jail, or the county's records and a word with the judge.
Duty: the sheriff answers to the voters, and the county's feuds and elections become yours.
police
A City Police Department
Once per case, patrol backup, a holding cell, or the department's files and crime lab.
Duty: the chain of command, the union's politics, and a department that resents Operants and ExLAW alike.
dire
DIRE
Once per case, military hardware, a medical team or a classified file.
Duty: DIRE's research comes first, and you may be part of it.
uniled
Interpol
Once per case, international reach: a Red Notice, a foreign police force's help, or a flight to anywhere.
Duty: member countries who want different things, and fugitives who know your face.
as
Affaires spéciales
Once per case, French intelligence, a safehouse in Europe or a discreet extraction.
Duty: France's interests, which aren't always yours.
legion
The New Power Legion
Once per case, a famous ally, a sponsor's money or the press on your side.
Duty: the sponsor's image, the schedule and the cameras.
knights
The Shadow Knights
Once per case, a relic, a specialist or a safe house of the Ordo.
Duty: the vow; bring light into the shadows, whatever the law says.
wardens
The Earth Wardens
Once per case, an Adept's help, ritual materials or lore.
Duty: guard the Earth Gates, and answer when the Wardens call.
haven
The Haven
Once per case, sanctuary in the Mad Forest, or the Green Man's attention.
Duty: protect the Earth and the Haven; and only vegetarian meals.
morcain
The Morcain
Once per case, money, a fence, a smuggling route or muscle.
Duty: the 12 take their cut, and send you their jobs.
reasons: Justice
The law should mean something, for Operants and everyone else.
Protection
Someone has to stand between ordinary people and what's out there.
Redemption
I've done things I'm not proud of. This is how I pay it back.
Fame
The cameras love an Operant, and I love the cameras.
Money
Powers pay. So does knowing who has them.
Revenge
Someone did this to me. I'm going to find them.
Freedom
No lab, no registry and no government owns me.
Truth
There's a story nobody's telling. I'm going to tell it.
Duty
I swore an oath, to a badge, an order or a god. I keep it.
Belonging
This team is the only place where I'm not a freak.
connections: Partners
We've worked cases together for years and trust each other with our lives.
They saved my life
They pulled me out of a burning building, a lab or a firefight.
I saved theirs
I got them out when no one else would, and they haven't forgotten.
Same wave
Our powers woke the same night, and we found each other afterward.
I arrested them
Once I put them in cuffs. Now we work together, uneasily.
Rivals
We want the same job, the same headline or the same collar.
Family
We're related, by blood, by marriage or by the same lab.
A shared secret
We know what really happened on that case. Nobody else does.
Mentor
They taught me how to use my powers, or how to survive without them.
An unpaid debt
I owe them money or a favor, and I haven't paid it yet.
advantages: +2 to Firearms after spending an action aiming at the same target.
+2 to Brawling when unarmed against more than one opponent.
+2 to Brawling to disarm, throw or restrain.
+2 to Melee with a chosen weapon.
+2 to Athletics to climb, leap or roll with a fall.
You can pilot an Aegis suit (Aegis Pilots are already certified); +2 to Piloting in one.
+2 to Investigation to read a crime scene or an Operant's traces.
+2 to Computers to break security or cover your tracks.
+2 to Engineering to jury-rig, repair or modify on the spot.
+2 to Medicine to stabilize a patient under fire.
+2 to Occult to recognize a creature, a curse or a ritual.
+2 to Law to make an arrest, a warrant or a confession stand up in court.
+2 to Streetwise to find a person, a rumor or a fence.
+2 to Persuasion to talk someone down.
+2 to Deception to pass as someone else.
+2 to Leadership to coordinate a team under fire.
+2 to Read People to spot a lie or a hidden Operant.
+2 to Media to spin a story or get one out.
+2 to Powers to use a power precisely: around bystanders, at a distance or delicately.
+2 to Deception to keep your two lives apart. Take the Secret Identity complication unless the GM agrees otherwise.
+2 to Will to keep acting under fire, fear or mind powers.
You start play with three dossiers, each a secret your work or your origin taught you: something in no database, registry or published record. They grant no bonus: they let you act on what you know.
complications: You live two lives. Accept the danger when someone gets close to the truth.
A warrant has your name or your mask on it. Accept the arrest attempt.
The Foundation, DIRE or someone worse wants you back. Accept the retrieval team.
Your powers flare when you're afraid or angry. Accept the collateral damage.
You don't kill, whatever they've done. Accept the cost of mercy.
The cameras follow you everywhere. Accept the attention at the worst moment.
The EPAOC or Internal Affairs is watching you. Accept the hearing.
You owe the 12, and they collect. Accept the job they send.
You have an enemy who won't stop. Accept their interference.
You put bystanders first, always. Accept the cost.
Someone you love doesn't have powers. Accept the threat to them.
Your anger gets ahead of you. Accept the fight you should have avoided.
You need something to keep going: Ambrosia, a lab's serum, a ritual's fuel. Accept the hunt for more.
You don't understand this world's rules, or it doesn't accept you. Accept the misunderstanding.
A spirit, a bond or a memory won't leave you alone. Accept the vision.
You lived through Chicago, 2012 or a lab when others didn't. Accept the reckless choice to make it right.
Your badge, order or sponsor gives you orders you don't like. Accept them.
A loose thread pulls you in. Accept the detour or the danger.
You jump first and think later. Accept the danger.

Someone volunteers to take your place

The careful plan takes too long

equipment: Fifteen rounds. Class I; hits mark 2 boxes.
Six shells. Class I. Within a few paces a hit marks 3 boxes and leaves the target Dying; farther away, 1 box.
Thirty rounds; can fire bursts. Class I; hits mark 2 boxes.
Twenty rounds; long range. Class I; hits mark 2 boxes.
Two shots. The target rolls Body −2: failure, out for the scene; success, −2 on their next action. Marks no box.
Class I melee: hits mark 1 box.
Once per fight, a Class I hit marks one box fewer.
A clear polycarbonate shield: +1 to Block against blows, thrown objects and missiles. It won't stop a bullet. −2 to Stealth while you carry it.
ExLAW issue: a cuffed Operant's powers drop one Class (two with a successful Engineering roll to tune them).
Federal, police or press credentials: open doors and get you past cordons.
Stay in touch with your team and dispatch.
Needed to stabilize a patient and give field treatment.
Needed for most Investigation at a crime scene.
Needed for most Computers work against secured systems.
Needed for most Engineering in the field, and for Aegis suit repairs.
Chalk, salt, candles, herbs: Class I ritual materials for a few workings.
Needed to pick locks with Engineering.
Record, broadcast, and get into press events.

Aegis Pilots or Aegis Certified only. While suited: Strength II, Toughness II, Flight I and a Class II arm cannon (Firearms). Takes a minute to suit up; a hit to the power pack (−2 to aim) can shut it down.
ExLAW issue for agents who face telepaths: Mind Defense II while worn. Obvious, and it hums.

tracks.name: Collateral
effects: Clean so far
Property damage: insurance claims and angry owners
Bystanders hurt: −2 to Media and Persuasion with the public
Lawsuits and charges: someone is held liable
An EPAOC hearing: start a clock; a team member may lose their status

tracks.name: Scrutiny
effects: Nobody's looking
Questions in a report
Flagged: −2 at checkpoints, cordons and with federal agencies
Investigated: ExLAW or the FBI opens a file on you
Hunted: the Foundation or Raster Zero takes an interest; start a clock

tracks.name: Backlash
effects: The public trusts you
Talk shows ask hard questions
Protests: −2 to Media and Leadership with crowds
Anti-Operant laws proposed; Operant friends blame you
Riots: the next case starts in a city that wants you gone

personalTrack.name: Strain
effects: Steady
Strained: −1 to Powers
Frayed: −2 to Powers; nosebleeds, sparks and flicker
Breaking: on a natural 16–18 with Powers the power goes wild
Burned out: your powers fail until you rest a full day

identityTrack.name: Exposure
effects: Safe: your secret is held only by those who already know it
Rumors: someone outside the circle wonders out loud
Suspected: someone outside the circle who matters is sure; −2 to Deception about who you are
Cornered: one more slip and it's out; the people close to you are being watched
Unmasked: the world knows. Choose the price: a loved one taken, your job or home lost, or a hunter on your trail

knownBy.label: Who knows
knownBy.intro: The people and groups who already know who you are. Exposure is how close the secret is to getting past them.
knownBy.placeholder: e.g. My sister Dana, the Legion's founders

byStatus.registered: The EMD (anyone with access to your file)

heroFiles.title: Villains' files
heroFiles.intro: What a villain knows about a hero: a weakness, a habit, a name, a loved one. When it applies, the villain gets the file's bonus against that hero. Heroes who find a file can see it on their sheet; when they destroy it, the bonus is gone.
heroFiles.knowsExample: Visits her mother at St. Agnes every Sunday

example.name: Wade Collier
example.role: Sheriff of a county whose southern line now ends at the Mad Forest. Awakened in the 1985 Second Wave at nine years old, and registered ever since.
example.reason: Someone has to stand between ordinary people and what's out there.
example.connection: Celerity asked him not to help the federal agents at the forest's edge. He's still deciding.

pregens.name: Rachel Kwan
pregens.role: Carries a jade seal that holds a guardian spirit, inherited from her grandmother. Her partner vanished on a case Director Humbacht closed personally.
pregens.reason: The law should mean something, for Operants and everyone else.
pregens.connection: Jess Calloway is the only reporter who asked about her missing partner. Kwan hasn't decided whether to trust her.
pregens.contact: Her missing partner's last informant, who only talks to her

pregens.name: Luis "Bulldog" Ortega
pregens.role: Twelve years in the suit, three of them in Iraq. The AS-6's new firmware came from a contractor nobody can trace, and lately the suit hesitates when he doesn't.
pregens.reason: Someone has to stand between ordinary people and what's out there.
pregens.connection: He flew cover for Rachel Kwan the night her partner vanished, and saw something he never put in the report.
pregens.contact: A DIRE engineer who still owes him for Basra

pregens.name: Naomi Price
pregens.role: The Legion's rising star, dosed with Ambrosia in a sponsor's clinic at nineteen. Her sponsor owns her image, her schedule and, she's starting to suspect, her secrets.
pregens.reason: The cameras love an Operant, and I love the cameras.
pregens.connection: Static saved her from a Foundation snatch team on live TV, and vanished before the cameras turned.

pregens.name: Dr. Tobias Wren
pregens.rank: Professor of comparative religion; Earth Warden
pregens.role: A collector of forbidden books who once traded a year of his life to something in Avalon for a translation. The year is coming due.
pregens.reason: Someone has to stand between ordinary people and what's out there.
pregens.connection: He taught Maeve Ashgrove's handler, and was the one who recognized what Maeve really is.

gear.item: The Lammas Grimoire, annotated in four hands
gear.use: identifying a curse, a ritual or a summoning from its traces

pregens.name: Jess Calloway
pregens.role: Touched a Raster Zero file in 2024 and saw the room it came from. Nobody knows she's an Operant; she's been pulling the thread ever since.
pregens.reason: There's a story nobody's telling. I'm going to tell it.
pregens.connection: Rachel Kwan's missing partner was her source. She hasn't told Kwan yet.

comp.trigger: Someone close asks where you were

pregens.name: Subject 19
pregens.role: Escaped a Foundation black lab a year ago with electric powers, no memory of a name, and a number tattooed on one wrist. Grachyov's retrieval team is still looking.
pregens.reason: No lab, no registry and no government owns me.
pregens.connection: Saved Daybreak from a Foundation snatch team on live TV, and ran before the cameras turned.

comp.trigger: A van with no plates outside

pregens.name: Maeve Ashgrove

pregens.reason: No lab, no registry and no government owns me.
pregens.connection: Dr. Tobias Wren saw through her glamour the first day. He's kept her secret; she wonders what it'll cost.

threats.label: Morcain enforcer (Operant)
threats.traitText: Arresting one makes the Morcain notice you (Scrutiny).

threats.name: White Hand soldier
threats.label: White Hand soldier
threats.traitText: Never surrenders, never talks.

threats.name: Foundation retrieval team
threats.label: Foundation retrieval team (minor)
threats.weaponText: Tranquilizer rifles; a dampening net (Power Negation II)
threats.traitText: They want the target alive, and leave no witnesses.

threats.name: Rogue Aegis suit
threats.label: Rogue Aegis suit
threats.traitText: Hit the pilot (−4) or the power pack (−2) to end it fast.

threats.name: Lab escapee
threats.label: Lab escapee
threats.traitText: On a natural 17–18, the power hits everyone nearby.

threats.name: Shadow Earth duplicate
threats.label: Shadow Earth duplicate
threats.traitText: Knows what the original knows; Mystic Sight reveals it. Use the original's numbers.

threats.name: Dubinsky werewolf
threats.label: Dubinsky werewolf
threats.traitText: Comes in threes; silver ignores its Defense.

threats.name: Fey raider
threats.label: Fey raider (Avalon)
threats.traitText: Iron weapons count one Class higher against it.

threats.name: Umkas soldier
threats.label: Umkas soldier
threats.traitText: Left behind in 2012; desperate and dangerous.

threats.name: Raster Zero hunter
threats.label: Raster Zero hunter
threats.traitText: No badge and no record; if caught, they never existed.

threats.name: Mad Forest wildwood
threats.label: Mad Forest wildwood
threats.traitText: Fire hurts it, but burning it brings the forest down on you.

threats.name: Mr. Marvel (Hector Gonzalez)
threats.label: Mr. Marvel (Hector Gonzalez) (Class IV)
threats.weaponText: Strength IV, electrical bolt, Blast IV
threats.traitText: As Hector Gonzalez he has no powers and Medicine 15. In the Marvel form his impatience and anger rise: a Will roll to walk away from a fight he's winning.

threats.name: Celerity (Ava Torres)
threats.label: Celerity (Ava Torres) (Class IV)
threats.traitText: Two actions a round, and a second defense. A federal warrant hangs over her: helping her marks Scrutiny.

threats.name: The Green Man (Micky Holt)
threats.label: The Green Man (Micky Holt) (Class V)
threats.weaponText: roots and thorns, Class IV in the Mad Forest, III outside it
threats.traitText: In the Mad Forest two wildwoods answer him each round he asks. Anyone who burns or harms the forest is the forest's enemy. Mad: what he wants changes with the song.

threats.name: Michael Lance
threats.label: Michael Lance (Class III)
threats.weaponText: a .38 revolver, Class I, the amulet's beam, Blast III
threats.traitText: Without the amulet he's a 1940s private eye with a revolver. Em Antu's spirit has its own opinions, and sometimes its own plans.

threats.name: Steel Hawk
threats.label: Steel Hawk (Class IV)
threats.weaponText: Strength III, spectral energy, Blast IV
threats.traitText: He must run every room he's in. Orders make him dig in; a deal that leaves him in charge can buy him for a while.

threats.name: Chat Roux (Red Cat)
threats.label: Chat Roux (Red Cat) (Class II)
threats.weaponText: dimensional sidearm, Class II, unarmed, Class I
threats.traitText: On a natural 17 or 18 with Deception, the mask flickers. Without repairs from his own Earth, one day it will fail for good.

threats.name: Vanguard ("Louis Feslen")
threats.label: Vanguard ("Louis Feslen") (Class III)
threats.weaponText: a manifested firearm, Class III, martial arts, Class I
threats.traitText: Wanted on four continents. If the rumor is true, every target was a Shadow Earth duplicate, and he knows how to spot them.

threats.name: Abd al-Rahman
threats.label: Abd al-Rahman (Class IV)
threats.traitText: Never alone: four Morcain enforcers' worth of mercenaries. Once a fight, he Teleports out with one passenger.

threats.name: The Golden Centurion
threats.label: The Golden Centurion (Class V)
threats.traitText: He clears a box every turn and comes back within an hour from anything, but he feels every wound. His code is iron: he never breaks his word, or forgives a broken one.

threats.name: The Shadow Knight (Grant Douglas)
threats.label: The Shadow Knight (Grant Douglas) (Class III)
threats.weaponText: consecrated blade, Class III, sidearm, Class I
threats.traitText: He brings his specialists: two or three ExLAW-grade operatives. Lose the artifacts and he's a very good ex-Marine.

threats.name: Lord Marrow (Altari Marrow)
threats.label: Lord Marrow (Altari Marrow) (Class III)
threats.weaponText: a living nightmare, Class II; Will resists
threats.traitText: A character with Will 13 or more resists his illusions at +2. He studies his victims first: if he knows your fear, the nightmare is Class III.

threats.name: The Ice Reaper (Hyun Wang)
threats.label: The Ice Reaper (Hyun Wang) (Class IV)
threats.weaponText: the Reaper's scythe of ice, Class IV, killing cold, Blast III
threats.traitText: In the Reaper's form he must take a life before the scene ends, or mark Strain. One of the 12: harming him draws the Morcain.

threats.name: Helios (David Carlysle Jones)
threats.label: Helios (David Carlysle Jones) (Class V)
threats.weaponText: solar blast, Class V, Strength III
threats.traitText: Eight hours without sunlight (not moonlight or starlight) and every power drops to Class I until he's back in the sun.

threats.name: Zephyr (Dr. Alemayehu Okafor)
threats.label: Zephyr (Dr. Alemayehu Okafor) (Class III)
threats.weaponText: a hammer of wind, Class III, Strength II
threats.traitText: Wanted in several countries. He spares workers and strikes machines; give him a polluter and he may become an ally.

threats.name: Evelyn Dark
threats.label: Evelyn Dark (Class V)
threats.traitText: On a natural 17 or 18 with Powers, the power hits everyone nearby. Using a power above Class III draws Avalon's hunters (Scrutiny).

threats.name: Milon Dubinsky
threats.label: Milon Dubinsky (Class IV)
threats.traitText: Silver ignores his Defense and stops his Regeneration. He never fights without three Dubinsky werewolves, and can't take human form.

threats.name: Nikola Tesla
threats.label: Nikola Tesla (Class VI)
threats.traitText: He arrives and leaves through a door from 1884 Ivry-sur-Seine. He has a way to trap the Atomic Man, and won't use it.

threats.name: The Atomic Man (Dr. Richard Kennedy)
threats.label: The Atomic Man (Dr. Richard Kennedy) (Class VI)
threats.weaponText: nuclear force, Class VI, Strength VI
threats.traitText: He won't risk a civilian, ever: put one in the line of fire and he stops. Only Grachyov has fought him to a draw.

traits.label: The Atomic Man (Dr. Richard Kennedy): quick

threats.name: Sergei Grachyov
threats.label: Sergei Grachyov (Class V)
threats.traitText: Reported dead several times. He's come for someone, never for a fight: hand over the escapee and he leaves.

threats.name: Uathach (Ciara Byrne)
threats.label: Uathach (Ciara Byrne) (Class IV)
threats.weaponText: the goddess's spear, Class IV, hand of red flame, Blast III
threats.traitText: The goddess is bloodthirsty: sparing a beaten enemy takes a Will roll. Ciara can't change back until the fight ends.

threats.name: The Ragged Magus (Dr. Elias Marron)
threats.label: The Ragged Magus (Dr. Elias Marron) (Class IV)
threats.weaponText: a crown of burning letters, Class III
threats.traitText: His ramblings hold a real clue each scene (a Read People or Occult roll to make sense of it). Threaten him and every pigeon in the tunnel answers.

threats.name: Autuarch
threats.label: Autuarch (Class VI)
threats.traitText: Never met alone: White Hand soldiers die for him without a word. He has escaped ExLAW three times; he always has a door open behind him.

gmGuide.title: Aurora GM's Guide
gmGuide.subtitle: Running the superhero setting: cases, notable Operants, threats and the GM's tools
gmGuide.intro: This book is for whoever runs the game. It gathers what the GM reaches for at the table: case seeds, the notable Operants of the world, the threats with their numbers, and how to use the GM view's battle map and Encounter panel. The rules themselves are in the **Players' Guide**; this book builds on them.
gmGuide.playersNote: The material for running the game (case seeds, the notable Operants, the threats, and the GM's tools) is in a companion book, the **GM's Guide**.

discovery.subject: an Operant's power set and its limits
discovery.uncover: the counter: the tell, the cost, the cooldown, what shuts the power down
phases: Effects without a cause: a vault opened from the inside, a blackout that follows someone, witnesses who can't agree on what they saw. You may suspect, but nothing is confirmed.

Name the Operant and what they can do. This is the gate: until its identity is confirmed, what you know about a kind of subject doesn't yet apply to this one, and your theories stay suspicions. You can still form hypotheses, test them and take ordinary precautions, and whatever is actually true of it works.

Find the counter: the tell before they act, what the power costs them, how long it takes to come back, what shuts it down. Filling this phase fills the clock and earns a dossier for what you established.

threat.name: Escalation
threat.onFill: the Operant's next move is bigger
threat.text: The Operant forces the pace. The Escalation clock (4 or 6 segments) ticks once for each scene spent investigating and once for each failed investigation roll. Each time it fills, their next move is bigger: a heist becomes a hostage situation becomes a fight across a city block. This is comic-book rising action, not a slow timer.

costs: digging publicly or drawing official attention
pulling federal files, flashing a badge you shouldn't, staking out in the open
provoking the Operant or their allies
leaning on their friends, taunting them on air, raiding their haunts
messy, public confrontations and property damage
forcing a test of the power in a crowd, a chase through traffic, breaking in
methods: Pattern of crimes, choice of targets, what they want.
EMD registry, ExLAW files, court records, hospital admissions.
Residue, readings, footage frame by frame, the physics or the magic of it.
Fences, fixers, who hired whom, who's scared.
Shadow them, test them, take the hit and watch what happens.
Viewer footage, tips, a reporter's notes. Always ticks Scrutiny on a failure.
discovery.origins: Some powers are methods in themselves: a telepath, a psychometrist or a power that senses energy can advance a phase with the Powers skill, at the GM's call.
routes: filled to the end of Uncover
watching the power used, or a careful test of it

sealed case notes, a former teammate's account, a lab's test results. A source's reputation alone doesn't make it right, but a reliable record can establish a fact without anyone repeating a dangerous test
what the Operant, or someone close to them, admits, supported by evidence
discovery.anyway: A real counter works whoever uses it, dossier or no dossier: if a power fails in the dark, it fails in the dark for anyone. Shutting a power down with equipment or a procedure still needs that equipment, the knowledge and the skill.
discovery.basis: street rumor and the tabloids, evidence, testimony, the team's own experience, or a suspicion they can explain
